mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 1.5% compresses discount rates and increases equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as monetary policy accommodates growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS remains below 1.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 4.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous housing starts (HOUST > 1500) and retail sales (RSAFS > 650000) indicate robust consumer demand, accelerating corporate revenue growth and generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of HOUST > 1500 and RSAFS > 650000 fails to produce positive returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100) during supply shocks reduces manufacturing output, increasing inflationary pressures and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: INDPRO decline below 100 fails to correlate with negative S&P 500 returns in more than 60% of supply shock instances.

mechanism_narrative: Positive quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1 > 1.5% annualized) indicates expanding economic activity, boosting corporate profits and generating positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when GDPC1 growth exceeds 1.5%.

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL exceeding 3.5% year-over-year signals persistent inflation, triggering aggressive monetary tightening that reduces equity valuations and causes negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent high unemployment (UNRATE > 4.0%) and weak employment growth (PAYEMS growth < 0.1%) indicate labor market stress, reducing consumer spending and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of UNRATE > 4.0 and PAYEMS growth < 0.1% fails to produce negative returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising FEDFUNDS above 2.0% during monetary tightening cycles increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 2.0% during tightening cycles.
